newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish data show danger of c/a deficit receding.
newsitem.headline: Danish data show danger of c/a deficit receding.

text.p: Better than expected Danish current account and trade figures show that the danger of a deficit in the balance of payments is dwindling, analysts said on Monday.

Central bank governor Bodil Nyboe Andersen last month, calling for fiscal stringency in 1998, warned that despite positive developments the Danish economy rested on "a knife edge" and the current account surplus remained modest, compared to foreign debt of 320 billion crowns.

The national statistics office reported a February current account surplus of 2.9 billion crowns, compared to an average forecast of 1.5 billion and a trade surplus, excluding ships, of three billion crowns compared to an expected 2.1 billion.
"Strong agricultural exports and continued positive statements on pork sales are good signs for the balance of payments," Svenska Handelsbanken Chief Economist Bo Overvad told Reuters.

"If the positive news on agricultural and energy exports continues and at the same time the outlook for industrial exports improves, it could well lead us to upgrade our estimate for the 1997 current account," he added.
Svenska Handelsbanken is currently predicting a 1997 surplus of five billion crowns.
The surplus for the 12 months to the end of February 1997 was 12.4 billion.
Nykredit Bank's Henrik Asmussen said the figures showed no danger of rising imports and underlined the fact that the balance of payments was not a factor to worry the bond market.

"As it has now been clear for some time that there is no immediate danger of the current account going into the red, the balance of payments is no longer an issue for the bond market," he said. --Stig Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969659
